newsitem.title: USA: New York regulators set RG&E hearings.
newsitem.headline: New York regulators set RG&E hearings.

text.p: The New York State Public Service Commission said it has scheduled a series of open consumer education forums and public hearings to seek consumer views on an electric rate and restructuring settlement proposal filed for Rochester Gas and Electric Corp on April 8.

The proposal agreed to by the utility, Department of Public Service Staff and several other parties, was filed in response to the commission's efforts to restructure the electric industry in New York state.
RG&E's proposal would cover a five-year period from July 1, 1997, to July 1, 2002.

The plan would reduce overall rates during the period by a total of $81.4 million. In addition, RG&E would forego $22 million of incentives owed from prior rate agreements and lost revenues from flexible rate contracts under which certain large users of electricity were provided lower rates to remain on the system, the commission said.

It said most residential and small business customers would receive rate reductions, which would average about 2.5 percent; some might experience slight bill increases due to increases in the minimum monthly customer charge.
In April, the company said it would continue to cut residential rates by five percent.

Large industrial customers would receive rate reductions averaging 10 percent; other commercial and industrial customers would receive reductions averaging 4.5 percent. A retail access program that would allow customers to purchase energy from alternate suppliers would be phased in beginning July 1, 1998.
The commission said the utility will functionally separate its distribution, generation and regulated retailing functions.

It would also be allowed to invest $50 million in a structurally and legally separate unregulated retailing company. RG&E may also petition to form a holding company the settlement proponents have agreed to support.

The commission said it has scheduled three public statement hearings as opportunities for interested members of the public to comment on RG&E's proposed plan. Prior to each of the public statement hearings, Department of Public Service staff will conduct an informal one-hour consumer educational forum to provide the company's customers with information about the key issues being examined in connection with RG&E's restructuring and the rate plan proposal.

These sessions will beheld May 28 at the Ontario County Court House in Canandaigua, with the education forum starting at 1800 EDT/2200 GMT; and May 29 at the Monroe County Office Building in Rochester beginning at 1300 EDT/1700 GMT and 1800 EDT/2200 GMT.
